billPassed: Government business moved on schedule. Both whips' offices had the numbers by lunchtime, and the {yeas} to {nays} division surprised nobody who was counting.
{party} carried {bill} with room to spare. Members were seen leaving the lobby before the Clerk had finished reading the result.
A tidy vote on {bill}, {yeas} to {nays}. The opposition's objections were noted, for the record, by the people who keep the record.
billDefeated: A government bill fell on the floor of the House, {nays} to {yeas}. The whip's office is understood to have known by the morning. The minister, it appears, was not told.
{leader}'s office called the defeat of {bill} a procedural setback. Nobody else in the building called it that.
closeVote: The division on {bill} came down to the last names read. Members who had been paired were seen in the lobby; members who had not were seen running.
{yeas} to {nays}, and the Speaker reaching for the standing orders. Both whips' offices spent the evening finding out who had been where.
confidenceLost: {party} lost the confidence of the House on {bill}, {nays} to {yeas}. The Governor General is to be consulted in the morning, and the country after that.
The benches emptied in silence. {leader} left by the members' door without stopping for the cameras, which had been waiting since Tuesday.
confidenceLostHandover: {party} fell on {bill}, {nays} to {yeas}, and the Governor General has asked {opposition} whether it can command the House. It says it can. The arithmetic says it is close.
No election, for now: {opposition} takes the Treasury benches on the strength of a vote it did not expect to win and the government did not expect to lose.
confidenceSurvived: {party} survived on {bill}, {yeas} to {nays}. The whips are taking the credit. The backbench is taking the weekend.
A confidence vote the government won and the opposition will not regret forcing: every member's name is now on the record, and the record is being read.
rebellion: {count} {party} members voted against their own whip on {bill}. The whip's office says the dissent was expected. The dissenters say it was not discussed.
A revolt of {count} is not a crisis, the {party} whip told reporters, in the tone of someone who had counted on fewer.
playerRebelled: {name}, the member for {riding}, voted against the line on {bill}. The whip's office declined to comment, which in that office is a comment.
The vote will play well in {riding}, where {bill} was never popular, and less well in the corridor outside the whip's door.
playerToedLine: {name} voted with the party on {bill}, against loud opposition at home. {riding} will have questions at the next town hall, and the member will have an evening to prepare answers.
Loyal, and seen to be loyal: the whip's office noted the vote. So did the local paper in {riding}.
routine: A day on {bill} that went the way the order paper said it would. Members were home for dinner, or said they were.
Nothing moved on {bill} that was not meant to move. The gallery filed early.
absence: The member for {riding} was not in the chamber when {bill} came to a vote. A spokesperson cited constituency business. The whip's office cited nothing.
An empty seat is noticed in a close House, and the House is close. {name}'s office says the absence was cleared. The whip's office has not said with whom.
walkout: {count} members left the chamber together before the vote on {bill}, which carried in their absence. The Speaker noted the empty benches and the time.
A walkout is a message to the cameras, and the cameras were there. What it does to the count on {bill} is a question for the whips.
leak: Notes from a closed caucus on {bill} reached this paper within the hour. {leader}'s office has begun the usual search for the usual suspects.
Someone in the room wanted this read. The party line on {bill} is that there is no division in the party, which is what parties say.
townHall: A full hall in {riding}, and most of it had come to talk about {bill}. {name} took every question. Not every answer landed.
{name} went home to face the riding on {bill} and found the riding had prepared. Two placards were about something else entirely.
qpHit: {minister} did not have the answer on {issue} and said so, which was the honest option and the worst one. {name}'s question will be clipped by the evening.
A backbench question from {riding} did what the opposition front bench had not managed all week: it left {minister} looking at the Speaker for help.
qpParried: {name} pressed {minister} on {issue}. {minister} answered a different question with some fluency, and the Speaker moved on.
A sharp question from {riding} met a soft answer. The gallery scored it a draw, which in Question Period means the minister won.
qpLob: The question from {name} was the one the minister's office had written, and {minister} read the answer it had written to go with it.
A planted question grew into a planted answer. Government members thumped their desks on cue.
qpRiding: {name} used the riding's sixty seconds to put {issue} to {minister}, who promised to look into it. {riding} has heard that before and wrote it down anyway.
Not on the party's list and not on the minister's: {issue} got its hearing because the member for {riding} would not use the question for anything else.
quiet: The House sat, the House rose, and the parking lot was empty by four. The whips call that a good week; the gallery calls it a long one.
Committee rooms, corridor talk, and nothing on the order paper anyone would cross the street to vote on. Members went home early and the lobby correspondents went home earlier.
No rebellion, no close call, no leak worth the name. Somewhere in the building someone is counting that as a victory.
